request.spec:
A correction may not exceed what remains of the claim it corrects: the target's amount less the
amounts of the corrections already made against it (VOID or DELETED ones left out). A larger
correction is refused with an error on the form.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A correction may not exceed what remains of the claim it corrects: the target's amount less the
amounts of the corrections already made against it (VOID or DELETED ones left out). A larger
correction is refused with an error on the form.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the correction limit, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

The check is in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/ClaimService.java`, in `corrected()`, next to the existing rule that a correction must name a SETTLED claim of the same person. It works out what remains of the target claim: its amount minus the corrections already made against it, leaving out VOID and DELETED ones. A correction larger than that is refused with a 422 error. The existing claim form already shows that error, so I didn't change the front end, and a refused correction writes nothing to the store or the audit file.

The check runs both when a claim is added and when one is saved from the editor. When editing a correction, its own current amount is left out of the total, so re-saving it as it is isn't refused.

**Decision for you:** restoring a DELETED correction is not checked. If other corrections took up the remaining amount while it was deleted, restoring it can push the total over the limit. The request only covers the form, so I left restore alone. Adding the same check there is a few lines if you want it.
